claim_boundary: Unchanged candidate index; not independent O evidence and not a new admission.

source_items.candidate: Gate recovery interventions on estimated failure prevalence, recovery probability, and disruption probability rather than monitor AUROC alone.
source_items.scope: Tested HotPotQA/GAIA/ALFWorld agents with a binary trajectory critic and simple intervention policies; 50-task pilot estimates the intervention sign.
source_items.result: Offline failure prediction around AUROC 0.94 can coexist with end-task degradation up to about 26 percentage points; the p*r-(1-p)*d decomposition connects monitor detections to recovery benefit versus disruption cost.
source_items.uncertainty: Pilot estimates and intervention effects are setting-specific; this does not cover every recovery mechanism and has no independent reproduction in C10.

supersedes.reason: Same decision question, but C10 supplies a source-qualified primary-paper identity, sharper p/r/d decision rule, and current evidence/relevance assessment.

source_items.candidate: Evaluate calibrated failure detection together with deterministic invariants and actual rollback/rerun repair success.
source_items.scope: 2,823 committed episodes across three agent frameworks/multiple models, with learned telemetry monitoring, deterministic checks, and live rollback/rerun repair.
source_items.result: Reported AUROC is 0.872; cold-to-recalibrated transfer changes from 0.527 to 0.885; live repair succeeds 45% versus 16% resampling and raises task success from 52% to 73%.
source_items.uncertainty: The learned monitor requires deployment-specific recalibration; deterministic checks cover only mechanically verifiable invariants; released artifacts are author-side rather than independent replication.
